CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK OF UTILIZATION AND CONSERVATION IN MULTIFUNCTIONAL RESERVOIR MANAGEMENT: BALANCING SUSTAINABILITY

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)

ABSTRACT

High pressure on water storage such as lakes and reservoirs due to their diverse uses, results in a decline in the quality of their water functions. This study aims to develop a conceptual network framework from an environmental conservation perspective using the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem (WEFE) Nexus framework. The WEFE framework was developed qualitatively by analyzing studies on the utilization and management of multifunctional reservoirs and lakes, especially those in Indonesia. Some things that are considered are the interaction between water functions, existing management, and the quality of the water environment. Based on the study conducted, several findings were obtained, namely: all functions entrusted to reservoirs or lakes have the same level of importance, whether as power plants, fisheries cultivation, water storage for irrigation and ecosystem processes. Critical trade-offs were identified between hydropower regulation and environmental flows, and between food production intensification and eutrophication-driven water quality decline. Cascading ecological degradation—triggered primarily by unregulated aquaculture—was found to propagate across energy efficiency, drinking water safety, and biodiversity. The proposed WEFE involves 6 inter-related parts: Water, Energy, Food, Ecosystem Integrity, Governance, and Socio-Economic Drivers. Ecological integrity has been changed from being a separate and limiting factor and now becomes the basis for all reservoir functions. These findings show that ecological thresholds will need to be integrated into a cross-sectoral decision-making process and into adaptive governance structures to balance how resources are used with long-term conservation requirements.
